spots.s: The original 1870 boardwalk — four miles of ocean air, rolling chairs and world-class people-watching; the easiest first-date stroll at the shore.
Rides out over the ocean plus a 227-ft climate-controlled observation wheel — corny, gorgeous at night, and the most reliable date-closer in AC.
Climb 228 steps up New Jersey's tallest lighthouse for a skyline-to-inlet panorama and a story to tell at dinner.
A six-story wooden elephant standing in Margate since 1881 — take the guided tour up to the howdah; pure Jersey Shore weirdness.
Cobblestone lanes, dozens of little shops, paddleboats and a carousel around the lake — unhurried afternoon-date material in Galloway.
One of America's oldest wineries (1864) pouring tastings on the edge of the Pinelands — an easy, classy inland detour.
AC's flagship in the marina district — headline shows, the comedy club and Spa Toccare make it a full day-to-night plan.
The glassy north-Boardwalk tower — sky-high spa and pool floor, big-name residencies, and the beach right off the lobby.

spots.n: Hard Rock Live at Etess Arena
spots.s: 7,000-seat room that books legit hip-hop, R&B and rock tours all year — check the calendar before you pick your weekend.
The quiet-island antidote to the Boardwalk — wide sand, seawall sunsets and dolphins working the bar just offshore.
Still the rare free beach in New Jersey — no badge, no fee, just walk on with a towel anywhere along the boards.
The working bayside quarter where the fishing boats tie up — crab shacks, marina sunsets and zero casino carpet.
Eight-mile wildlife drive through salt marsh with the AC skyline floating behind the egrets — golden-hour photography gold.
Open-air outlet blocks threaded between the casinos — useful rainy-hour filler that occasionally coughs up a real deal.
Three revived blocks off the boards — beer hall, rock club, taco patios — where AC's actual local scene hangs out.
The residential, vendor-free stretch of boards — sunrise walks with locals and the best quiet-mile conversation setting downbeach.
Stockton University's downtown gallery-and-studio hive with rotating shows and a folk-art museum — free, air-conditioned culture.
Brigantine's seal-and-dolphin rescue outfit since 1978 — a small museum with a big story, right before the seawall.
A quiet sculpture garden of inscribed granite columns off Pacific Avenue — a reflective ten minutes most visitors never find.

nightlife.s: Ocean's two-level big room with international DJs inside and a summer beach club on the sand — AC's splashiest dance floor.
Borgata's 18,000-sq-ft club regularly booking hip-hop and open-format names — dress up and commit to the night.
Harrah's swim-up party around an 86,000-gallon pool — Friday and Saturday mayhem with celebrity-host sets.
Tropicana's unapologetic throwback club — 70s/80s Friday–Saturday plus a 90s/2000s Thursday that's secretly the best dance-floor value in town.
Orange Loop rock room booking punk-to-hip-hop tours, plus the PASS/GO house-and-techno night every second Thursday.
Cajun kitchen up front, DJs and a big patio out back — the Orange Loop's late-night living room.
Ocean's casino-floor lounge where live bands and DJs trade sets and the dance floor actually gets used — no cover.
Glass-roofed beer garden with 90s arcade cabinets and two live stages — loud, casual, zero dress code.
Golden Nugget's free live-music bar with bands most nights — a no-cover warmup around a 360-degree bar.
Free live sets nearly every night in the middle of the casino floor — Hard Rock's front row to its live-music-365 promise.
Toes-in-the-sand beach bar on the boards at Resorts — summer cover bands, buckets and sunset margaritas.
Creaky turn-of-the-century barroom pouring cheap pints around the clock — the best conversation room in Atlantic City.
24/7 local dive with famous wings — where the dealers and bartenders drink after their shifts.
Somers Point's handsome Irish pub with weekend live music — the anchor of the bayfront bar crawl.

eats.s: Borgata's slick izakaya — robata skewers, pristine sushi and a sake list built for a second round.
Hard Rock's quiet fine-dining Japanese room — imported fish, wagyu and real omakase energy; book it when the night matters.
Margate's dependable sushi-and-hibachi house — solid nigiri and rolls without the casino markup.
Margate's Cal-Asian staple with a serious sushi bar — half restaurant, half see-and-be-seen scene.
Bayside Margate institution — oysters, a proper martini and live piano; the reliable big-date move.
Family-run since 1897 — oysters, fat crab cakes and old-AC service; the definitive date dinner downtown.
The flatiron landmark from 1912 serving chops and lobster in Prohibition-era rooms — history you can taste.
Basement BYOB legend — veal chops, banana cream pie, and a reservation that's half the flex.
The 1946 sub counter that fed Sinatra — split a White House Special with someone you like.
Ducktown red-gravy since 1935 — homemade ravioli and photos of three generations of regulars on the walls.
Thin-crust tavern pizza and a bar that barely closes — the correct 1 a.m. decision since 1927.
Soul-food supper club on Pacific Avenue with live R&B, jazz and neo-soul most nights — dinner that turns into a night out.
Little Saigon's roomiest pho hall on Atlantic Avenue — restorative broth for the morning after the clubs.
Gardner's Basin breakfast shack beloved for blueberry pancakes on the water — earn them with an early walk.
Deck seats over the marina, crab pretzels and sunset beers — casual date insurance at Gardner's Basin.

chinese.s: Borgata's pan-Asian noodle room — hand-pulled bowls, dim sum bites and Cantonese BBQ, open late for the tables crowd.
Hard Rock's street-food counter running Cantonese, Sichuan and Vietnamese bowls — the best quick 面 fix on the Boardwalk.
Golden Nugget's kitchen beside the Asian gaming pit — Cantonese and Szechuan standards plus sushi, cooking late into the night.
Atlantic City's oldest Vietnamese kitchen (1990) — broken-rice plates and roast meats with deep Chinese-Vietnamese roots.
Named for the Teochew-style hủ tiếu it does best — the Chinese-Vietnamese noodle soup worth crossing town for.
Ventnor Avenue hole-in-the-wall pho — short menu, deep broth, neighborhood prices.
Arctic Avenue's Little Saigon grocery — fish sauce to fresh herbs, the shelves the neighborhood's kitchens actually shop.
The area's biggest Asian supermarket, out on the Black Horse Pike — live seafood, a proper produce wall and every Sichuan pantry staple.

fishing.s: AC's own back-bay party boat out of Gardner's Basin — two fluke trips daily plus Friday-night bites; NJ saltwater takes only the free registry, no license.
Somers Point's family-run half-day head boat (8a and 1p sailings) drifting the bays for flounder and sea bass — easy, social, beginner-proof.
Brigantine six-pack charters working back-bay stripers, fluke and tog — the serious small-group option when you want the cooler full.
Route 30 bait shop with guided back-bay trips and everything for a crabbing run — the local intel stop before any outing.
Classic pier off the boards at Cornwall Avenue — kingfish, blues and croakers all season for a small pier pass; free saltwater registry covers you.
Free 24/7 promenade along the inlet — stripers, tog and blues in the rips within sight of the casino lights.
Rock piles at Great Egg Inlet that light up during the fall bunker runs — bucktails, moving tide, watch the birds.
Drive-on 4x4 beach (city permit) with miles of open surf — the area's best shot at a sunrise striper, free registry only.
Where the Mullica River meets Great Bay — famous for New Jersey's earliest keeper stripers every spring; walk-on and free.
Quiet Northfield ponds holding bass, pickerel and stocked trout — freshwater does need the state license, unlike the salt.

biking.s: JORBA-maintained pine-flat singletrack looping 1,700 county acres — the closest real mountain-bike ride to the island.
Tight, twisty loops around the old lake in a 220-acre reserve — short but legit, minutes off the Parkway.
Endless Pine Barrens sugar-sand roads rolling out from Batsto Village — honest gravel adventure, bring wide tires and a map.
900 acres of surprisingly rolling Pines singletrack up the Parkway — the best real terrain within an hour.
7.5 smooth car-free miles from Harbor Square to Mays Landing under the pines — the no-stress road spin.
Pedal the boards from the inlet clear through Ventnor — flat, breezy and iconic; bikes get the boards until noon in season.

social.s: Tropicana's late-night Latin party with pro salsa dancers working the floor — arrive early for dinner and you've built the whole date.

social.n: DJ Trivia at Tennessee Ave Beer Hall
social.s: Forty taps and league-style trivia in the Orange Loop's living room — join a team that's short a player and you've made friends.
Free Friday concerts on William Morrow Beach — bring a chair and a cooler; the whole bayfront turns out.
Free all-paces 5K on the boards from Ocean Casino Resort — warm-up at 8:15, coffee conversation after.
Half-hour recitals on the world's largest pipe organ plus a peek backstage — a genuinely great cheap date.
Eighty-plus vendors packing the St. James lot — the Friday-morning social hour downbeach.
Island market with Hammonton blueberries, bagels and shaved ice — a chatty Saturday-morning loop.
Forty vendors spilling out of the Steve & Cookie's lot on the bay — Margate's midweek meet-up.
Hour-long all-levels flow on the sand by the Ventnor pier — $15, salty air, friendly crowd.
